s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly growing caruncular lesion with ulceration
salient_findings: Amelanotic, pedunculated mass with ulcerated surface
Large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
key_facts: 4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
Lesion is amelanotic and pedunculated with an ulcerated surface
Lesion arises from the caruncle
No evidence of primary acquired melanosis (PAM)
Specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm with a 4-mm ulceration
Necrotic tissue present on the surface of the specimen
Solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface
Large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
Positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
Significant number of cycling cells shown by Ki-67 proliferation marker
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma of the caruncle
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly growing amelanotic pedunculated mass with ulceration, positive reactivity to melanocytic markers

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ulcerated lesion with rapid growth, although less likely given the specific immunohistochemical findings

shortlist.label: Sebaceous gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in the caruncle, a site with sebaceous glands, and rapid growth pattern

shortlist.label: Mucosal melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similarities with the presented case, including ulceration and rapid growth, although less specific to the caruncle

shortlist.label: Nodular melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth and ulceration, consistent with nodular melanoma characteristics, and positive melanocytic markers

raw.rationale: The lesion's rapid growth, amelanotic and pedunculated appearance with an ulcerated surface, and positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A support this diagnosis. The absence of PAM and the specific location of the lesion on the caruncle also align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Mucosal Melanoma
rejected.why: While mucosal melanoma can occur in the conjunctiva, the specific details provided do not exclusively point to this diagnosis over malignant melanoma of the conjunctiva.

rejected.label: Nodular Melanoma
rejected.why: Nodular melanoma typically refers to a subtype of skin melanoma and does not specifically relate to the conjunctival location described in the case.

rejected.label: Conjunctival Melanocytic Tumor
rejected.why: This term is broader and could encompass benign or malignant lesions, but the aggressive features described (rapid growth, ulceration, high mitotic activity) suggest a malignant process, making Malignant Melanoma of the Conjunctiva more specific.

rejected.label: Lentigo Maligna Melanoma
rejected.why: Lentigo maligna melanoma is a type of skin melanoma that typically occurs on sun-damaged skin, which does not match the conjunctival location of the lesion in this case.
